defects_cross_referenced.title: Overnight batch 'complete' notification reports $0.00 spent on a Redis ledger read failure, even though the real spend is correctly persisted elsewhere in the same code path
defects_cross_referenced.source: orchestrator-filed (team-lead), independently re-discovered here via code reading before I knew D-17 existed -- CONFIRMED DUPLICATE, not a new filing per team-lead correction 2026-07-18
defects_cross_referenced.root_cause: src/lib/queue/batch-digest.ts processBatchDigestJob(), ~line 199: the db.bookNotification.create() message string is built from the raw ledger.spentUsd (which readBatchLedger defaults to 0 on any Redis read failure), instead of the already-computed effectiveSpent variable that the db.batchRun.update() call two lines below correctly uses. Z11 (commit c9e99e7) fixed the persisted BatchRun.spentUsd and digest JSON to use the DB-fallback effectiveSpent, but missed this second read of the same ledger object.
defects_cross_referenced.contribution: New regression-lock test tests/unit/batch-digest-notification-spend.test.ts (mirrors Z11's existing test scenario plus a notification-message assertion). Run via npx vitest run tests/unit/batch-digest-notification-spend.test.ts -> FAILS (RED): AssertionError: expected '2/2 passes . $0.00 / $10.00 cap' to contain '$6.00'. BatchRun.spentUsd assertion in the same test passes (effectiveSpent correctly resolves to $6.00) -- isolates the defect to the notification-message read specifically. Offered to team-lead as D-17's regression lock.
